01:
In East Uusimaa, 15 breast sessions mean 16 round trips and 45 road hours for a Myrskylä patient (96 km from Helsinki) [S60, S59].

1. The HUS head of radiation oncology could evaluate a single 8 Gy session as default for uncomplicated painful bone metastases (equal pain relief, more retreatment) [S31, S30, S62]. Myrskylä: 2.4 expected round trips instead of 6.2 [S60, S59, S30]. HUS treats this county [S36]. Its bone page mentions pain relief but no number of sessions [S65]. First step within 30 days: the bone team decides [S31, S62]. Goal 3 indicator: National targets and key effectiveness indicators defined for agreed cancers [S61].

2. The breast team lead could evaluate 5 sessions, non-inferior to 15, as default for eligible patients (whole breast or chest wall, no nodal radiotherapy), naming distance as a reason [S9, S11, S15, S14]. Myrskylä: 6 round trips, 17 road hours [S60, S59]. County: about 28 patients a year would avoid 282 round trips and 475 road hours [S33, S57, S34, S35, S60]. First step within 30 days: the team reviews eligibility and decides [S15, S14]. Goal 3 indicator: Patients receive treatment within target times [S25, S24].

3. The cancer quality lead could publish schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band yearly, as palliative use falls with distance [S21, S27]. First step within 30 days: clinical leads agree what to count, as the current mix is not public [S16]. Goal 3 indicator: Regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services [S26].

Limitations: centre-point distances, population-based patient allocation and an assumed schedule mix [S59, S57, S60, S16].
